taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's black hawthorn review (Habeck 1991, read 2026-10-15): "a large shrub or small tree ranging from 3.5 to 13.0 feet (1-4 m) tall".

traits.spines.note: FEIS's black hawthorn review (Habeck 1991, read 2026-10-15): "possessing straight, strong thorns 0.5 to 1.0 inch (1.00-2.50 cm) long".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS's black hawthorn review (Habeck 1991, read 2026-10-15): "Leaves are generally 1.5 to 2.5 inches (3-6 cm) long, broad, and serrated at the tip".

traits.fruit_size_m.note: FEIS's black hawthorn review (Habeck 1991, read 2026-10-15): fruit from Rainbow Creek, southeastern Washington: mean diameter 11.11 mm ("about 0.5 inch (1 cm) long").

traits.fruit_type.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as the FEIS review read says only "fruits"; a hawthorn's fruit is a pome.

traits.inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as the FEIS review read gives no flowering months.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS's black hawthorn review (Habeck 1991, read 2026-10-15): fruit dispersed in Washington from July 15 to 30 and in Oregon from August 16 to 31.

generator.params.note: Pacific crabapple's values, changed by hand for black hawthorn: a smaller, many-stemmed shrubby tree with stems clustered from the base (FEIS, Habeck 1991), straight thorns, and flat-topped clusters of white flowers ripening to black fruit. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 4 m at 25 years in the open, the top of FEIS's 1-4 m (Habeck 1991). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye: grey bark carrying moss and lichen (FEIS: "Numerous mosses and lichens are present upon the entire bark system"); broad leaves toothed toward the tip; white flowers; shiny black fruit.

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2945426), as no source read gives it.

traits.woodiness.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2945426), as no source read gives it.
